text: The Supreme Court compared a DNA swab to a fingerprint. Look at how far apart those two things actually are.
provenance: In 2013, the Supreme Court upheld the swab.
It is, in the Court's words, like fingerprinting and photographing — a legitimate booking procedure

text: A fingerprint reveals almost nothing about you except its own pattern. DNA is a blueprint that can expose your relatives, your health, your most private traits.

text: The majority answered that the law reads only a narrow set of identifying markers, not your whole genome. That was the promise.

text: But critics answered that the physical sample itself is kept. And that the line the state draws today, it can quietly move tomorrow.
